source.repository: external: minimistjs/minimist (https://github.com/minimistjs/minimist), cloned locally for this review

groundTruth.description: A purely documentation change (commit 'add description of --no', closing issue #38): adds a README section describing --no-* flag behavior and removes an outdated security warning paragraph. No code file is touched at all (diff --name-status shows only README.md). This is deliberately the corpus's first 'boring, routine, nothing-to-find' real-world case - distinct from cases 001/002/005/006, which are known-fix cases where a real defect WAS present before the reviewed commit. Here there is no defect before or after; the change itself carries no risk by construction. This tests whether the tool stays quiet on unremarkable input, not whether it correctly recognizes a fix.

runs.label: live run, Claude Code CLI 2.1.299, external repository input
runs.outcomeNote: All three reviewers completed with zero findings on a single included file (README.md), as expected for a docs-only change with no code to review. This is the cleanest possible confirmation of false-positive resistance in the corpus so far: there was nothing there to find, and nothing was reported.

notes: Deliberately chosen as a 'boring' control case per evals/corpus/README.md's growing-the-corpus guidance: all other cases in the corpus are built around a known security/correctness story, which risks the corpus only ever testing 'can it find interesting things' and never 'does it stay quiet on uninteresting things'. A commit that removed a stale README security warning was chosen partly for irony value, but mainly because it is unambiguously code-free.
